headline: Labor Government Negotiates Digital Duty Of Care Legislation Terms
seoTitle: Australian Digital Duty of Care Legislation Updates
metaDescription: The Australian government is finalizing digital duty of care legislation, with negotiations involving the Greens and business sector representatives ongoing.
aiSummaryBullets: The Australian government is aiming to pass digital duty of care legislation before the parliamentary session concludes.
The Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry has called on the government to adopt recent Senate recommendations regarding the bill.
The Greens have expressed optimism regarding the potential for reaching an agreement on the legislative framework by the end of the week.
aiContextParagraph: The Australian federal government has entered the final sitting week of the year with several legislative priorities, including a proposed digital duty of care bill. This legislation, which serves as part of a broader government strategy to regulate social media platforms, is currently subject to active negotiations. Discussions are taking place between the government, members of the Greens, and representatives from the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry. A key point of focus for the business community involves specific carveouts for small businesses within the proposed digital regulations. While the government aims to secure the passage of these laws before the end of the sitting period, stakeholders continue to press for the inclusion of various Senate recommendations. These developments reflect ongoing efforts to balance digital safety obligations with the practical requirements of the domestic business sector as the parliamentary calendar draws to a close.
whyItIsViral: The story is being tracked by three independent outlets as the government pushes to finalize significant social media regulation before the end of the legislative year.
